q-148735.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{x}.$
q-148735.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{x}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{y}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt[3]{y} \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =-\frac{3}{2}x \\ (\sqrt[3]{y})^{3} & ={(-\frac{3}{2}x)}^{3} \\ y & =-\frac{27}{8}{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=-\frac{27}{8}{x}^{3}.
$$

q-148734.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{x}+3.$
q-148734.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{x}+3
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y}+3.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y}+3 \\ \frac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{y} & =x-3 \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =2(x-3) \\ (\sqrt[3]{y})^{3} & ={(2(x-3))}^{3} \\ y & =8(x-3)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=8(x-3)^{3}.
$$

To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{x}}-3
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{y}}-3.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{y}}-3 \\ \frac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{y}} & =x+3 \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =\frac{5}{2(x+3)} \\ {(\sqrt[3]{y})}^{3} & ={(\frac{5}{2(x+3)})}^{3} \\ y & =\frac{125}{8(x+3)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{125}{8(x+3)^{3}}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x\ne 0,\,f(x)\ne -3.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x\ne -3,\,{f}^{-1}(x)\ne 0.
$$

q-148745.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=5-\frac{3}{8\sqrt{x}}.$
q-148745.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=5-\frac{3}{8\sqrt{x}}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=5-\frac{3}{8\sqrt{y}}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5-\frac{3}{8\sqrt{y}} \\ x-5 & =-\frac{3}{8\sqrt{y}} \\ \sqrt{y} & =-\frac{3}{8(x-5)} \\ (\sqrt{y})^{2} & ={(-\frac{3}{8(x-5)})}^{2} \\ y & =\frac{9}{64(x-5)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{9}{64(x-5)^{2}}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are given by

$$
x>0,\,f(x)<5.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x<5,\,{f}^{-1}(x)>0.
$$

q-148557.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2x-3}}.$
q-148557.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2x-3}}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2y-3}}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2y-3}} \\ \sqrt[3]{2y-3} & =\frac{2}{x} \\ {(\sqrt[3]{2y-3})}^{3} & ={(\frac{2}{x})}^{3} \\ 2y-3 & =\frac{8}{{x}^{3}} \\ 2y & =\frac{8}{{x}^{3}}+3 \\ y & =\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{3}{2}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x\ne \frac{3}{2},\,f(x)\ne 0.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x\ne 0,\,{f}^{-1}(x)\ne \frac{3}{2}.
$$

q-148290.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{2x+3}-4.$
q-148290.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\sqrt[3]{2x+3}-4
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\sqrt[3]{2y+3}-4.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\sqrt[3]{2y+3}-4 \\ \sqrt[3]{2y+3} & =x+4 \\ (\sqrt[3]{2y+3})^{3} & =(x+4)^{3} \\ 2y+3 & =(x+4)^{3} \\ 2y & =(x+4)^{3}-3 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}(x+4)^{3}-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}(x+4)^{3}-\frac{3}{2}.
$$

The function $f(x),$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\frac{2}{3\sqrt{x+k}}+5,\,x>-k
$$

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{4}{9(x-5)^{2}}-2,\,x>5.
$$

What is the value of $k?$

$$
y=\frac{2}{3\sqrt{x+k}}+5
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{2}{3\sqrt{y+k}}+5.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt{y+k}}+5 \\ x-5 & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt{y+k}} \\ \sqrt{y+k} & =\frac{2}{3(x-5)} \\ {(\sqrt{y+k})}^{2} & ={(\frac{2}{3(x-5)})}^{2} \\ y+k & =\frac{4}{9(x-5)^{2}} \\ y & =\frac{4}{9(x-5)^{2}}-k\end{aligned}
